steps.summary: A comprehensive introductory programming course covering fundamentals from variables to object-oriented design.

steps.name: Getting Started
steps.intro:
Week 1: Getting Started

Welcome to Introduction to Programming! This week we set up our development environment and write our first program.

steps.name: Course Overview
steps.intro: Read the full course overview including objectives, schedule, and assessment criteria. This course takes you from zero programming experience to building your own applications.

steps.name: Variables & Data Types
steps.intro:
Week 2: Variables & Data Types

Learn about integers, strings, floats, and booleans. Understand how computers store and manipulate data.

steps.name: Coding Exercise: Variables
steps.intro: Write a program that declares variables of different types (integer, float, string, boolean) and performs basic operations with them. Submit your source code file.

steps.name: Control Flow
steps.intro:
Week 3: Control Flow

Master if/else statements, loops (for, while), and switch/case structures to control program execution.

steps.name: Coding Exercise: Control Flow
steps.intro: Write a program that uses conditional statements and loops to solve a series of problems. Include at least one for loop, one while loop, and nested if/else logic.

steps.name: Functions
steps.intro:
Week 4: Functions

Learn to write reusable code with functions. Understand parameters, return values, and scope.

steps.name: Discussion: Code Reusability
steps.intro: Share your thoughts: Why are functions important in programming? Give an example from your own experience where breaking code into functions made it easier to understand or maintain.

steps.name: Arrays & Lists
steps.intro:
Week 5: Arrays & Lists

Work with collections of data. Learn about arrays, lists, and common operations like sorting and searching.

steps.name: Coding Exercise: Arrays
steps.intro: Write a program that creates an array of at least 10 elements, sorts them, searches for a specific value, and calculates the average. Submit your source code.

steps.name: Object-Oriented Programming
steps.intro:
Week 6: Object-Oriented Programming

Introduction to classes, objects, inheritance, and encapsulation. Design your own data structures.

steps.name: Coding Exercise: OOP Basics
steps.intro: Design a class hierarchy for a simple library system. Create classes for Book, Member, and Library with appropriate attributes, methods, and relationships. Submit your source code.

steps.name: Project Work
steps.intro:
Week 7: Project Work

Apply everything you have learned to build a complete application. Work independently or in pairs.

steps.name: Final Project
steps.intro: Build a complete application of your choice that demonstrates variables, control flow, functions, arrays, and at least one class. Include a README explaining your design decisions. This is worth 40% of your final grade.

steps.name: Course Review
steps.intro:
Week 8: Course Review

Review key concepts, ask questions, and prepare for the final assessment.

steps.name: Course Feedback & Questions
steps.intro: Use this forum to ask any remaining questions about the course material, share resources you found helpful, or provide feedback on the course.
